name: Rich Purple
lede: Rich purple is a deep, reddish purple, and the phrase is older as a description than as a name: books use it for the purples that glazes and dyes could make.

sections.title: A phrase before a name
sections.body:
In the books this color shows up as description rather than a fixed term. Ball notes that a red lake glaze over a blue ground turns it to a rich purple, a trick of fifteenth-century oil painting [1]. The same book remarks that van Dyck did not seek the rich purple-red one might expect from Titian [2].

In dye history the phrase attaches to older purples. Murexide, made from guano, is called a rich purple by Garfield [3]. St Clair tells of a Florentine merchant who brought back lichen dyeing from the Levant and made a rich purple of the kind once reserved for costly murex [4]. His family's change of name to Ruccellis is told as a story, so treat it with care [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: At #720058 the swatch is dark and strongly red-leaning, closer to [[plum]] and [[mulberry]] than to [[violet]] [5]. Four book mentions use the words, none as a standard color name [1][2][3][4].

notes.cite: St Clair, The Secret Lives of Colour, "Orchil"

questions.q: What glaze over a blue ground gives a rich purple?
